newsitem.title: GERMANY: BA raises cargo rates from Germany.
newsitem.headline: BA raises cargo rates from Germany.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo will raise ex-Germany air cargo rates by up to 10 percent from March 1, Mark Gardiner, cargo manager Central Europe, said
Gardiner said: "One of the reasons why we decided to increase rates is to ensure German forwarders have more opportunity for more space on BA routes."
Even though the new rates still did not take the stronger pound fully into account, they gave BA in Germany a better chance of winning space on ex-London intercontinental flights, he added.
Airline offices in different countries compete for space on planes flying on long haul routes from their national hub to meet yield targets.
"The strength of the pound has made the internal fight (between different BA cargo centres) for capacity more difficult for BA in Germany," Gardiner said.
"I think forwarders will accept the higher rates, there is an understanding that rates need to be pushed up," he added.
The increases were also a reaction to local market conditions but did not fully take the rising exchange rate of the British pound into account, Gardiner stated.
Rates to North Atlantic and Middle East destinations would rise by 10 percent across the board, he told Reuters in an interview.
In Asia, prices for India, Japan, China, Singapore and South Korea would be raised by up to 10 percent, he added.
Selected Africa destinations, including Johannesburg, Harare and Lagos, would also have price hikes of up to 10 percent.
But rates to South America, the Caribbean and other Asian destinations would be held at present levels, he said. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+ 5017
